cues.en: All companies store data from a simple record book of a small business, maybe even on a journal or a piece of paper.
cues.zh: 所有公司都會儲存資料，從小企業簡單的記錄簿，甚至日誌或紙張，

cues.en: To massive companies like Amazon that need computers to store petabytes of data.
cues.zh: 到 Amazon 這樣的大公司，需要電腦儲存 PB 等級的資料。

cues.en: Now, in order to store this information, pretty much every company and sometimes individuals, too, need something called a database.
cues.zh: 為了儲存資訊，幾乎每家公司，有時連個人，都需要資料庫。

cues.en: We saw in the last section how hard it was to have our server remember a new user.
cues.zh: 講者在這段沿用前一節的例子：要讓伺服器記住新使用者，很不容易。

cues.en: Every time the server crashed, the variable would get reset and then it would start all over.
cues.zh: 每次伺服器當掉，變數就重設，一切得重來。

cues.en: Or if we wanted to do a login or a sign in check and iterate through the emails and passwords doing a loop through JavaScript, that's inefficient.
cues.zh: 要檢查登入或註冊，如果用 JavaScript 迴圈逐一比對電子郵件與密碼，效率也不好。

cues.en: That's where database come to the rescue.
cues.zh: 這時資料庫就能幫忙。

cues.en: So let's ask ourselves, what is a database?
cues.zh: 問問自己，什麼是資料庫？

cues.en: A database is a collection of data.
cues.zh: 資料庫是資料的集合。

cues.en: And what we mean by data.
cues.zh: 這裡說的資料，

cues.en: There are many forms of them, right?
cues.zh: 有很多形式，對吧？

cues.en: There can be numbers, there can be dates, there could be password hashes.
cues.zh: 可能是數字、日期、密碼雜湊。

cues.en: There could be user information.
cues.zh: 也可能是使用者資訊。

cues.en: Databases allow us to organize this data in a way that is useful to us, and it makes data management easy.
cues.zh: 資料庫讓我們以有用的方式組織資料，使管理更容易。

cues.en: And something came out of that and it's called database management system or DB MBS for short.
cues.zh: 因此出現資料庫管理系統，簡稱 DBMS。

cues.en: It's a collection of programs which allows us to access databases and work with data, and it also allows control access to database users.
cues.zh: 它是一組程式，讓我們存取資料庫、操作資料，也控制使用者對資料庫的存取權。

cues.en: So a db mbs is something in this box.
cues.zh: DBMS 就是這個框裡的東西。

cues.en: Something that allows us a tool, a piece of software that allows us to communicate.
cues.zh: 一個工具、一套軟體，讓我們能夠，

cues.en: With the database store information that's useful for us and also allows us to update, insert, delete,
cues.zh: 與資料庫溝通，儲存有用的資訊，也能更新、插入、刪除，

cues.en: lookup, whatever is in the database.
cues.zh: 查詢資料庫裡的內容。

cues.en: And this idea of a DB PBMs really started to take shape in 1960s, and now it is at the forefront of many exciting things.
cues.zh: DBMS 的概念在 1960 年代開始成形，如今是許多令人興奮技術的核心。

cues.en: There's an entire industry of engineers that just work with databases because it is so important.
cues.zh: 有整個工程師產業專門處理資料庫，因為它太重要。

cues.en: Now there are two types of DMS that are really popular right now and that we're going to talk about in this course.
cues.zh: 現在有兩類很受歡迎的 DBMS，這段課程會介紹。

cues.en: And these two types are represented really well by Post Gress and MongoDB.
cues.zh: PostgreSQL 與 MongoDB 很能代表這兩類。

cues.en: Let's talk about the first one, which is relational database.
cues.zh: 先談第一類：關聯式資料庫。

cues.en: And this is probably the most popular as you can see on the right hand side, you see that all of these are relational databases, post grass, Oracle, SQL Server.
cues.zh: 可能也是最常見的類型；右邊這些都是，例如 PostgreSQL、Oracle、SQL Server。

cues.en: You may have heard of MySQL SQL Light.
cues.zh: 也可能聽過 MySQL、SQLite。

cues.en: These are all types of databases that have this relational database tag to them.
cues.zh: 這些都屬於關聯式資料庫。

cues.en: And the beauty with them is that they're all pretty much similar.
cues.zh: 好處是它們大致相似。

cues.en: They all follow a same standard format.
cues.zh: 遵循相同的標準格式。

cues.en: Relational databases consist of two or more tables with columns and rows.
cues.zh: 講者將關聯式資料庫描述為，由兩個以上包含列與欄的資料表組成。

cues.en: So in this case, users is a table and full name username text created at our columns and whatever values they have here are rows.
cues.zh: 這裡 users 是一張表，full_name、username、text、created_at 是欄，底下每筆值是一列。

cues.en: Each row represents an entry and each column sorts a very specific type of information like name, address or phone numbers.
cues.zh: 每列代表一筆項目，每欄儲存特定類型的資訊，例如姓名、地址、電話。

cues.en: And then the relation between tables and field.
cues.zh: 資料表與欄位之間的關係，

cues.en: It's called a schema in a relational database.
cues.zh: 在關聯式資料庫裡稱為 schema，也就是結構描述。

cues.en: The schema must be clearly defined before any information can be added.
cues.zh: 新增資訊前，schema 必須先明確定義。

cues.en: And if this is confusing right now, don't worry, we're actually going to create these databases.
cues.zh: 現在覺得困惑也沒關係，接下來會實際建立資料庫，

cues.en: So it makes sense to you.
cues.zh: 讓你理解。

cues.en: If we had Twitter, for example, you can see over here the types of tables that we would have and how we would organize it.
cues.zh: 例如 Twitter，可以看到可能會有哪些資料表，以及如何組織。

cues.en: We would have a user stable, a tweet table, a following table.
cues.zh: 有 users、tweets、following 等表。

cues.en: And we can connect all these information, for example, by connecting different pieces of the table.
cues.zh: 可以透過表裡不同的欄位，把這些資訊連起來。

cues.en: For example, the username will be the same in the user's table as it is in the tweet.
cues.zh: 例如 users 表與 tweets，

cues.en: Stable.
cues.zh: 表裡，會有相同的 username。

cues.en: That way we can say that the username in the tweets table is the foreign key of the username in the
cues.zh: 如此就能說，tweets 表的 username 是對應到，

cues.en: user's table and then from user.
cues.zh: users 表 username 的外鍵。接著 from_user，

cues.en: Will be the foreign key of username in the following table.
cues.zh: 在 following 表中，也透過外鍵對應 username。

cues.en: Now things like full name or ID, something that identifies each row in a table.
cues.zh: 像 full_name 或 ID，能識別表中每一列的欄位，

cues.en: It's called a primary key, and we'll go through that later on in the section.
cues.zh: 講者稱為主鍵，後面還會談。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So all these databases we're going to learn about PostgreSQL, but they're all pretty much the same.
cues.zh: 我們會學 PostgreSQL，不過這些資料庫大致相似。

cues.en: So once you know one, it's fairly easy to pick up the other ones.
cues.zh: 熟悉一種後，學其他的也相對容易。

cues.en: How do they actually communicate with a server with the backend?
cues.zh: 它們實際如何與伺服器、後端溝通？

cues.en: Well, all relational databases use something called SQL.
cues.zh: 關聯式資料庫使用 SQL。

cues.en: And SQL allows us to communicate just like HTTP did between the front end and the back end with SQL.
cues.zh: SQL 讓我們溝通，就像 HTTP 用來連接前端和後端，透過 SQL，

cues.en: We're able to communicate with the database and modify or get or update however we want.
cues.zh: 則能與資料庫溝通，修改、取得、更新資料。

cues.en: And we'll have a video on this topic as well.
cues.zh: 也會有影片介紹這個主題。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So that's relational databases.
cues.zh: 這就是關聯式資料庫。

cues.en: What about the second type?
cues.zh: 第二類呢？

cues.en: The second type is called a non relational database or a NoSQL database.
cues.zh: 第二類叫非關聯式資料庫，或 NoSQL 資料庫。

cues.en: And once again, there are many, many different types of databases with some cool names like Couch DB and Hyper Table.
cues.zh: 同樣有很多類型，還有 CouchDB、Hypertable 等有趣名字。

cues.en: Now a MongoDB or a non relational database lets you build an application without having to define the schema first.
cues.zh: MongoDB 這類非關聯式資料庫，讓你不必先定義 schema，就能建立應用程式。

cues.en: Unlike a relational database.
cues.zh: 這和關聯式資料庫不同。

cues.en: If we go back to relational database, this schema or these tables have to kind of be predefined, right?
cues.zh: 回頭看關聯式資料庫，schema 或資料表通常必須事先定義，對吧？

cues.en: We need to know how our app is going to look, make these tables so that once the app is public, we
cues.zh: 需要知道應用程式的結構，建立這些表，讓應用程式公開後，

cues.en: can start entering user information and tweets and followers.
cues.zh: 就能開始寫入使用者、推文、追蹤者資訊。

cues.en: With a no SQL or non relational database, we can just define it as we go and they all have different ways of storing this information.
cues.zh: NoSQL、非關聯式資料庫則可邊做邊定義，各自也有不同的儲存方式。

cues.en: So each one is very, very different.
cues.zh: 所以每種可能差很多。

cues.en: And this is another powerful reason to use a non relational database is that if your data requirements aren't clear at the outset of your project and maybe you have a massive amount of unstructured data,
cues.zh: 這也是使用非關聯式資料庫的一個重要理由：專案開始時，資料需求若不清楚，或有大量非結構化資料，

cues.en: you may not have the luxury of developing a relational database with a clearly defined schema.
cues.zh: 可能無法先設計好明確 schema 的關聯式資料庫。

cues.en: They offer instead a greater flexibility in that a non relational database are more like folders just assembling related information of all types.
cues.zh: 非關聯式資料庫提供更大彈性，有點像資料夾，把各種相關資訊放在一起。

cues.en: Now MongoDB is something called document oriented.
cues.zh: MongoDB 是所謂文件導向的資料庫。

cues.en: It's stores information as documents.
cues.zh: 以文件形式儲存資訊。

cues.en: Let me illustrate this point to you.
cues.zh: 示範一下。

cues.en: I have my desktop here with two folders.
cues.zh: 桌面上有兩個資料夾。

cues.en: One is a relational database and here I have users tweets, profile following.
cues.zh: 一個代表關聯式資料庫，裡面有 users、tweets、profile、following。

cues.en: And you can think of relational databases with this type of storage where this folder lives somewhere on a computer that stores this information.
cues.zh: 可以把它想成某台電腦裡，存放這些資訊的資料夾。

cues.en: And any time we need to ask a database for something, well, we grab the users.
cues.zh: 要向資料庫查詢時，先取得 users。

cues.en: And if we also want to grab the tweets of the user, we find the user that we're interested in, then
cues.zh: 如果還想找某位使用者的推文，先找到該使用者，

cues.en: find the tweets of the user that we're also interested in with the foreign key that links to the users.
cues.zh: 再透過連到 users 的外鍵，找出他的推文。

cues.en: And we can also find however many followers that user has.
cues.zh: 也能找出他有多少追蹤者。

cues.en: We grab that information and display it on our web app.
cues.zh: 取得資訊，再顯示在網路應用程式上。

cues.en: MongoDB, on the other hand, will actually have each user as a document.
cues.zh: MongoDB 則可以把每位使用者存成一份文件。

cues.en: So if I wanted to grab the first user, well, I just grabbed this document and it has all the followers, the tweets, the profile, everything is in this one document.
cues.zh: 要取得第一位使用者，直接取這份文件，裡面有追蹤者、推文、個人資料，全部在同一份文件。

cues.en: And you might be thinking, hmm, MongoDB looks like a better choice than having this.
cues.zh: 你可能想，嗯，MongoDB 看起來比較好，

cues.en: Way of doing things right.
cues.zh: 比那種做法方便，對吧？

cues.en: Well, it depends on your need.
cues.zh: 其實取決於需求。

cues.en: And that's why databases is such a complex topic.
cues.zh: 這就是資料庫很複雜的原因。

cues.en: It really, really depends on your situation.
cues.zh: 真的要看情境。

cues.en: You can see this MongoDB way being very useful if you have something like a profile, maybe a LinkedIn
cues.zh: 例如個人資料、LinkedIn，

cues.en: profile, but if you needed something where you're working with just following data or just tweets data, maybe with the tweets you want to see, what is the average tweet size?
cues.zh: 個人檔案，用 MongoDB 這種方式很方便；但如果只處理追蹤資料或推文，想知道平均推文長度，

cues.en: Well, it's really easy to just grab this file and calculate that versus this way where you might have to extract it from each one of the users.
cues.zh: 直接取得 tweets 的資料就容易計算；另一種做法可能要從每位使用者的文件擷取。

cues.en: So it really depends on your needs.
cues.zh: 所以取決於需求。

cues.en: Let me show you another diagram that might be.
cues.zh: 再看另一張可能有，

cues.en: Useful.
cues.zh: 幫助的圖。

cues.en: When we look at relational versus non relational databases, you can think of relational as each table
cues.zh: 比較關聯式與非關聯式時，可以把關聯式想成各張資料表，

cues.en: has a blog post, a blog tag, a blog comment, and it links these tables to give you the blog information
cues.zh: 分別存部落格文章、標籤、留言，再把它們連接，取得部落格資訊。

cues.en: versus a non relational that stores this entire blog post in an entry and has comments, tags, categories and all other related data just in one single place.
cues.zh: 非關聯式則把整篇文章存成一筆，留言、標籤、分類及其他相關資料，都放在同一處。

cues.en: So what does MongoDB use to communicate?
cues.zh: MongoDB 使用什麼來溝通？

cues.en: If we go back to our example here, we had SQL for relational databases such as Post Press.
cues.zh: 回到範例，PostgreSQL 等關聯式資料庫用 SQL。

cues.en: Well, MongoDB has its own what we call query language, and it is just the MongoDB query language.
cues.zh: MongoDB 則有自己的查詢語言，就叫 MongoDB Query Language。

cues.en: But they both aim to do the same thing.
cues.zh: 但兩者目的相同。

cues.en: That is, to communicate with the database, provide an easy way for the server to communicate with the database.
cues.zh: 與資料庫溝通，提供伺服器容易使用的溝通方式。

cues.en: And in this section, we're going to be talking about that and we're going to finally connect the dots and show you the power of databases once they're connected to a server.
cues.zh: 這一節會談這些，最後串起概念，展示資料庫連上伺服器後的能力。

cues.en: I'll see you in the next one.
cues.zh: 下一支影片見。
